text:
Priya Patel: Heads up — after the gpu-operator 1.8.0 rollout we started seeing driver installs fail on a subset of nodes (RHEL/CentOS kernel builds). Pods stuck in CrashLoopBackOff and kubelet reports module signature errors.
Priya Patel: example from node gpu-rt-07:
```
Feb 16 03:12:18 kernel: nvidia: module verification failed: signature and/or required key missing - tainting kernel
Feb 16 03:12:18 dkms: ERROR: Cannot install module nvidia-525 for kernel 5.14.0-300.el8.x86_64: Required key not available
```
Priya Patel: gpu-operator daemonset logs show the installer exits with code 1, then kubelet marks the node as NotReady while the kmod probe fails. Seeing scheduling backoffs on large GPU jobs.
Ryan Chen: ugh. was that the operator that enabled module signing enforcement? @Priya any chance it came from the new init-hook that calls rpm --ignoresign?
Priya Patel: yeah, operator 1.8 enabled stricter install path that relies on pre-signed kernel modules. We didn't catch this on our fedora/centos pool because their kernels differ from the ubuntu images in the canary.
Alex Morales: does this affect NCCL or just driver load? If modules don't load, multi-gpu jobs will fall back and time out.
Priya Patel: modules don't load -> nvidia-smi returns no devices -> pods fail at container init. NCCL processes time out once they try to enumerate GPUs.
Sam O'Neill: I'm oncall — cordoning the affected nodes now and scaling down any queued GPU jobs. Can we roll operator back?
Priya Patel: recommended immediate action: 1) cordon affected nodes, 2) rollback gpu-operator to 1.7.x, 3) add a node selector label to keep fedora/centos nodes on older driver path for now.
Maria Gomez: +1 for rollback. Also we should avoid a full cluster-wide rollout until we have a signed-module fallback or automated signing in our image build pipeline.
infra-bot: [action] node cordon started for nodes: gpu-rt-07,gpu-rt-08,gpu-rt-09 by Sam O'Neill
Ryan Chen: quick rollback plan: patch the operator deployment image to 1.7.4 and apply. command: `kubectl -n gpu-operator set image daemonset/gpu-operator gpu-operator=ghcr.io/redwood/gpu-operator:v1.7.4` then watch daemonset rollout.
Priya Patel: note: the driver-installer job may leave partial dkms state. After rollback we might need to run cleanup on nodes: `dkms remove -m nvidia -v 525 --all` and then re-trigger driver install via the operator.
Alex Morales: is there any workaround to sign modules on the node (can we import a test key)? That could be a short-term mitigation for critical nodes.
Maria Gomez: we discussed keys earlier — we don't have a centralized signing key for fleet kernels. Injecting keys requires updating grub and mokutil, which is disruptive. Not a good emergency fix.
Sam O'Neill: Rollback in progress. Deploy-bot: `rolling back gpu-operator to v1.7.4`
deploy-bot: deployment gpu-operator rolled back to ghcr.io/redwood/gpu-operator:v1.7.4 (replicas updated)
Sam O'Neill: nodes are coming back healthy, kubelet shows modules loading again on the first two nodes after cleanup. Still verifying NCCL runs.
Priya Patel: creating an infra ticket to track long-term fix: either add signed-module fallback in the operator or add a gating e2e that includes fedora/centos kernel variants. Ticket: INFRA-1782
Ryan Chen: action owners: Priya -> lead triage + cleanup instructions; Alex -> test NCCL perf on recovered nodes; Maria -> coordinate signing strategy with security. Sam -> follow-up incident postmortem.
Alex Morales: quick test result: single-node cuda job OK, NCCL micro-bench shows multi-GPU handshake failing on gpu-rt-09 (probably leftover dkms). Re-running cleanup and re-bootstrap.
Priya Patel: update: after dkms remove + reinstall via operator 1.7.4, node gpu-rt-09 passed. I've uncordoned gpu-rt-07/08/09.
Maria Gomez: good. We should add a preflight check in rollout pipeline to validate module build + probe on all distro pools.
Sam O'Neill: adding to oncall checklist: if operator enables module signing, gate on MOK presence and dkms success.
Priya Patel: will follow up with a short runbook and the INFRA-1782 ticket. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Ryan Chen: thanks — keep me posted if any nodes relapse, I'll keep the rollback image pinned in the staging operator repo until we have the fix.
